questions.question: What should you expect in a C++ interview?
questions.shortAnswer: If you're preparing for a C++ interview, expect questions ranging from fundamentals (syntax, memory management) to advanced topics like templates, STL, and multithreading.

questions.question: What are the beginner-level C++ interview questions (C vs C++, struct vs class, new vs malloc, references, overloading)?
questions.shortAnswer: C++ adds object-oriented features (classes, inheritance, polymorphism) to C. … By default, members of a `struct` are public, while members of a `class` are private. … `new` calls constructors and returns typed pointers; `malloc` just allocates raw memory.
followUps: What is C++ and how is it different from C?
What is the difference between `new` and `malloc`?
Explain function overloading vs operator overloading.

questions.question: What are the intermediate-level C++ interview questions (shallow vs deep copy, virtual functions, stack vs heap, templates, exceptions)?
questions.shortAnswer: Shallow copy duplicates only pointers; deep copy duplicates the actual data. … Virtual functions enable runtime polymorphism; pure virtual functions (`=0`) make a class abstract.
followUps: What is the difference between shallow copy and deep copy?
Explain virtual functions and pure virtual functions.
What is the difference between stack and heap memory?

questions.question: What are the advanced-level C++ interview questions (RAII, vector vs list, map vs unordered_map, multithreading, compile-time vs runtime polymorphism)?
questions.shortAnswer: What is RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization)? A design principle where resources (memory, file handles) are tied to object lifetime.

questions.question: What are the key C++ differences to remember side by side?
questions.shortAnswer: `struct` vs `class` | Default access: public vs private … `new` vs `malloc` | Constructor call vs raw memory … `map` vs `unordered_map` | Ordered O(log n) vs Hash O(1)

questions.question: What are the main risks and best practices in C++?
questions.shortAnswer: Memory leaks: Always pair `new` with `delete`, or better use smart pointers (`std::unique_ptr`, `std::shared_ptr`).
pitfalls: Memory leaks: Always pair `new` with `delete`, or better use smart pointers (`std::unique_ptr`, `std::shared_ptr`).
Multiple inheritance: Can cause ambiguity (diamond problem); use virtual inheritance carefully.
Templates: Powerful but can lead to code bloat if misused.
Exception safety: Always ensure destructors are `noexcept` to avoid undefined behavior.
